title: SPH3U Exit Card Learning Package
problemAnchor: 本节课的核心概念（Vector Concepts and Displacement、Speed and Velocity）之间有什么联系？学生在理解上最容易卡在哪里？

knowledgeNodes.name: Vector Concepts and Displacement

knowledgeNodes.ossdExpectation: Demonstrate an understanding of uniform and non-uniform linear motion, in one and two dimensions.

questions.stem: A person walks 5 m east, then 12 m north. What is the displacement from start to finish?

options.label: A
options.feedbackWrong: That's the total distance, not displacement. Displacement is a vector from start to end.

options.label: B
options.feedbackWrong: Check the Pythagorean theorem; 5 and 12 give a larger resultant.

options.label: C
options.feedbackWrong: Direction is not purely east; it is northeast (or at an angle).

options.label: D
options.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! Displacement magnitude is 13 m and direction is northeast.

questions.stemIntent: Distinguish between speed (scalar) and velocity (vector) by computing average velocity in a round trip.

questions.stem: A car travels 100 m east in 10 s, then 100 m west in 10 s. What is its average velocity?

options.label: A
options.feedbackCorrect: Yes! Net displacement is 0 m, so average velocity is 0 m/s.

options.label: B
options.feedbackWrong: That's the average speed, but velocity also considers direction. The net displacement is zero.

options.label: C
options.feedbackWrong: Same as B; net displacement is zero.

options.label: D
options.feedbackWrong: That's the total distance divided by total time, which gives speed, not velocity.

questions.stem: On a position-time graph, a straight line passes through (0 s, 0 m) and (10 s, 100 m). What is the slope of this line?

options.label: A
options.feedbackWrong: Slope is rise over run: (100 m - 0 m) / (10 s - 0 s) = 10 m/s.

options.label: B
options.feedbackCorrect: Exactly! Slope = 100 m / 10 s = 10 m/s, which is the average velocity.

options.label: C
options.feedbackWrong: You might have divided time by position. Slope is position change over time change.

options.label: D
options.feedbackWrong: That's time over position (10/100). Slope is position over time.

reteachModules.trigger: student adds magnitudes of vectors without considering direction or omits direction in velocity/displacement answers
reteachModules.studentMisunderstanding: The student treats displacement as a scalar (distance) and ignores direction when adding vectors or computing velocity.

miniLesson.explain: Displacement is a vector: it has both magnitude (how far) and direction (which way). When adding displacements, you must consider direction. For example, 5 m east plus 2 m east equals 7 m east, but 5 m east plus 2 m west equals 3 m east (not 7 m). Always include a direction in your answer.
miniLesson.example: A car travels 700 m west, then 100 m east. The net displacement is 600 m west (since 700 west minus 100 east = 600 west). If you simply added the magnitudes, you would get 800 m, which is the total distance, not the displacement.
miniLesson.memoryAnchor: Direction is non-negotiable! Always ask: 'Where is the tip pointing?'

guidedPractice.prompt: A person walks 5 m east, then 2 m east. What is the displacement?
A cyclist rides 700 m west, then 100 m east. What is the displacement?
A runner goes 43 m east, then 28 m west, then 11 m east. What is the net displacement?

reteachModules.trigger: Student uses total distance instead of displacement when calculating average velocity, or treats velocity as scalar.
reteachModules.studentMisunderstanding: You may be confusing speed (a scalar quantity) with velocity (a vector quantity). Speed only cares about how fast an object is moving, while velocity also includes the direction of motion. When calculating average velocity, you must use displacement (change in position, with direction) rather than total distance traveled.

miniLesson.explain: Speed is a scalar that measures how fast an object moves, calculated as total distance divided by time. Velocity is a vector that measures the rate of change of position, including direction, calculated as displacement divided by time. For example, if a dog runs 43 m in 28 s, its average speed is 43/28 ≈ 1.54 m/s. But if it runs 43 m east and then 43 m west back to start, its displacement is 0 m, so average velocity is 0 m/s (even though speed is positive).
miniLesson.example: A car travels 100 m east in 10 s, then 100 m west in 10 s. Average speed = total distance (200 m) / total time (20 s) = 10 m/s. Average velocity = displacement (0 m) / total time (20 s) = 0 m/s. The velocity is zero because the car ended up where it started.
miniLesson.memoryAnchor: Remember: 'Velocity is displacement per time; speed is distance per time.' Think of the 'dis' in displacement for 'direction included'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Select the vector quantity from the list: speed, distance, velocity, time.
A cyclist travels 120 m east in 60 s, then 60 m west in 60 s. What is the average velocity?
guidedPractice.answer: Displacement = 120 m east - 60 m west = 60 m east. Total time = 120 s. Average velocity = 60 m east / 120 s = 0.5 m/s east.

guidedPractice.prompt: A runner runs 700 m north in 120 s, then 700 m south in 120 s. What is the average velocity?
guidedPractice.answer: Displacement = 0 m (since north and south cancel), total time = 240 s, average velocity = 0 m/s.

reteachModules.trigger: Student incorrectly calculated velocity without converting km to m.
reteachModules.studentMisunderstanding: Student fails to convert between units (e.g., km to m) before performing calculations, leading to incorrect numerical results.

miniLesson.explain: Unit consistency is essential in physics calculations. You must convert all quantities to the same unit (e.g., meters, seconds) before applying formulas. For example, if distance is given in kilometers and time in seconds, convert kilometers to meters (1 km = 1000 m) before calculating speed or velocity.
miniLesson.example: A cyclist rides 2 km east in 120 s. To find average velocity in m/s, first convert 2 km to 2000 m, then divide: 2000 m / 120 s = 16.7 m/s east.
miniLesson.memoryAnchor: Remember: Just as you can't add apples and oranges, you can't mix units. Convert everything to the same unit first!

guidedPractice.prompt: A car travels 2 km in 120 s. What is its average speed in m/s?
A person walks 700 m east, then 2 km west. What is the net displacement? Then find the average velocity if total time is 120 s.
guidedPractice.answer: Convert 2 km to 2000 m. Net displacement = 700 - 2000 = -1300 m (1300 m west). Velocity = 1300 m / 120 s = 10.8 m/s west.

reteachModules.trigger: Student miscounts slope or confuses slope with another quantity on Q4.
reteachModules.studentMisunderstanding: Student may misinterpret position-time graph slope as speed rather than velocity, or fail to relate slope to displacement and time.

miniLesson.explain: On a position-time graph, the slope (rise over run) equals the average velocity. Velocity is a vector, so direction matters: positive slope means motion in the positive direction, negative slope means opposite direction. Speed is the absolute value of velocity.
miniLesson.example: A line from (0 s, 0 m) to (5 s, 100 m) has slope = (100 m - 0 m) / (5 s - 0 s) = 20 m/s. This is the average velocity. Since the slope is positive, direction is positive (e.g., east).
miniLesson.memoryAnchor: Slope = speed? No! Slope = velocity (includes direction). Remember: 'Slope is velocity, speed is absolute.'

guidedPractice.prompt: On a position-time graph, a line passes through (0 s, 0 m) and (5 s, 100 m). What is the slope?
A position-time graph shows a line with slope -10 m/s. What does that tell you about the object's motion?
guidedPractice.answer: The object is moving at a constant velocity of 10 m/s in the negative direction (e.g., west).

guidedPractice.prompt: An object moves from position 0 m to 43 m in 28 s. What is its velocity? Then it moves back to 0 m in 28 s. What is the average velocity for the whole trip?
guidedPractice.answer: First segment: velocity = 43 m / 28 s ≈ 1.54 m/s positive. Whole trip: displacement = 0 m, so average velocity = 0 m/s.

questions.stem: A car travels 120 m north, then 60 m south. What is the car's displacement?
A person walks 5 m east, then 2 m west. What is the displacement? Be sure to include direction and magnitude.
questions.rubric: Correct answer: 3 m east. Must include both magnitude and direction.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
A person walks 100 m east in 60 s, then 100 m west in 60 s. Calculate the average speed and average velocity. Show your work.
questions.rubric: Average speed = total distance (200 m) / total time (120 s) = 1.67 m/s (or 1.7 m/s). Average velocity = displacement (0 m) / total time (120 s) = 0 m/s. Must recognize that velocity includes direction (though zero). Full credit for correct calculations and distinction between distance and displacement.

retestCards.passRule: Q1: Select 'Velocity'. Q2: Provide average speed = 1.67 m/s and average velocity = 0 m/s, with correct reasoning.

questions.stem: A car travels 5 km in 600 s. What is the correct first step to find the average speed in m/s?
A runner covers 2 km in 120 s. Calculate the average speed in m/s. Show your work.
questions.rubric: Correct conversion: 2 km = 2000 m (1 mark). Correct calculation: 2000 m / 120 s = 16.7 m/s (1 mark). Final answer with unit (1 mark).

retestCards.passRule: All questions must be answered correctly. For open-ended, answer must include correct conversion and numerical value.

questions.stem: A position-time graph shows a straight line from (0 s, 0 m) to (5 s, 100 m). What does the slope of this line represent?

A position-time graph for a car moving in a straight line is a straight line from (0 s, 0 m) to (5 s, 100 m) in the eastward direction. Calculate the slope of this line and explain what it means about the car's motion.
questions.rubric: Correct slope calculation: (100 m - 0 m) / (5 s - 0 s) = 20 m/s. Correct interpretation: The slope represents the car's average velocity, which is 20 m/s eastward. (Accept 'velocity' or 'average velocity'; mention direction or sign.)

retestCards.passRule: Student must answer Q1 correctly (select 'Velocity') and in Q2, correctly compute the slope as 20 m/s and state that it represents velocity (or average velocity).
